post.summary: Ingest, read, or compile context briefs
post.description:
Save and reuse evidence in an authorized Recoup workspace. **Preview: this reference is verified against API source, not a completed hosted acceptance test.** Actions require the corresponding database and workflow release; verification actions also require their feature to be enabled. Do not infer provider readiness, complete coverage, or a successful workflow from an accepted request schema.

### Create context

`ingest` creates or reuses a Spotify-track request and dispatches its durable workflow (202). The parser recognizes YouTube URLs, but ingestion still rejects them in this pilot. `ingest_release` stores a Spotify album locator; it does not automatically verify the release. `ingest_catalog` and `ingest_artist` refer to accessible Recoup records. `ingest_songwriter_name`, `ingest_company_name`, `ingest_campaign_brief`, and `ingest_supporting_text` store submitted context (200). Names and customer text are not verified identities or facts. Reuse an idempotency key only for the same intended input.

### Read, plan and inspect

`read` reads one request. For saved supporting text, HTTP and standard MCP also return a metadata-only `material_evidence` receipt identifying the current document, result and exact retained source version. It returns no submitted text, source location or signed access. `draft_origin` remains `not_recorded`: a retained customer assertion is not proof of its file origin or reviewed business facts. Unavailable material withholds those references. Delegated OAuth keeps its request-only response. `plan` plans modules from stored context; a plan is not authorization to collect data. `list_executions` and `read_execution` expose execution records. `list_catalog_members` pages saved members; `expand_catalog_members` materializes a bounded member page. These operations return 200. Request IDs, subject IDs and execution IDs refer to different records; use the IDs returned by the corresponding read rather than substituting an account ID. Catalog membership does not establish rights ownership. Use `plan_catalog_members` to plan a lookup for a page of current expanded catalog recordings, as described below.

### Plan a catalog lookup

A catalog manager can inspect which lookup would be proposed for recordings already expanded from an accessible catalog. This action reads the saved targets and returns a plan; it does not fetch recording matches, linked works or platform information.

Supply the existing catalog Context `request_id` and its catalog `subject_id`, one `module`, and optionally `organization_id`, `after_isrc` and `limit` (1–100, default 100). These IDs refer to different records: do not substitute the catalog ID, account ID or a member recording subject for the catalog Context subject.

| Preferred input | Lookup being planned | Legacy accepted input and returned module |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recording_candidates` | Unconfirmed recording candidates from an ISRC; a candidate is not an approved recording identity | `musicbrainz` |
| `recording_work_candidates` | Candidate works linked to a recording; no ownership or royalty-share verification | `mlc_recording` |
| `platform_metadata` | Available platform track information; no growth-metric or complete-coverage promise | `songstats` |

All six input values remain accepted. The three values in the last column are compatibility identifiers, not a promise that data sources are interchangeable. Each preferred/legacy pair returns the same page, raw module, executor, node key, state and reasons. Source and saved-plan provenance remain unchanged.

The 200 result is `ContextCatalogPlanningResponse`: `page`, `plan` and `collectionPermitted: false`. `page` includes `catalogId`, `catalogSubjectId`, `members`, `nextCursor` and `hasMore`. Each member retains `subjectId`, `kind`, `identityConfirmed`, `availableFields`, `reusableModules` and `isrc`. The saved ISRC-backed target flag does not verify an external recording match, rights or ownership. Only expanded recordings still present in the selected workspace's accessible catalog are returned; removed and not-yet-expanded members are excluded. Pass `page.nextCursor` as `after_isrc` when `page.hasMore` is true.

`plan` has one node per returned member, including `key`, `entry`, `subjectId`, `targetKind`, `module`, `executor`, `state`, `reasons`, `dependsOn`, `scope` and `executionStarted`. Node keys retain `{subjectId}:{legacy_module}`. This action supplies no permitted modules and does not reuse collection permission: every returned node is `blocked`, has `executionStarted: false`, an empty `dependsOn` and the reason `Server collection policy has not permitted this module`. An empty member page returns `plan: []` and still has `collectionPermitted: false`.

An executor name describes a planned implementation; it does not make that collector runnable. In particular, the platform-metadata collector is not connected to the trusted planned dispatcher. No provider/model call, execution claim, credit charge, new access grant or automatic catalog expansion is triggered. An accepted request or local fixture is not hosted customer-workflow acceptance.

### Release verification and review

`verify_release` and `verify_release_tracks` enqueue enabled verification workflows (202); disabled features or unmet readiness conditions return 409. `list_release_tracks`, `read_release_track_observations`, and `review_release_track_identities` inspect saved slots and identity evidence (200). Inspect the returned readiness, coverage and unresolved identity state before using a recording match. `list_release_cases`, `read_release_case`, `read_release_case_review`, and `review_release_case` read or record release-case review. A review requires the current fingerprint, a decision, and an idempotency key; it does not silently rewrite source evidence.

### Compile and save briefs

`brief` compiles evidence from up to ten completed or partial requests in one workspace without provider or model calls. Purposes are `creative_direction`, `playlist_pitch`, and `company_onboarding`. Creative direction prioritizes lyrics and artwork; playlist pitching prioritizes catalog/audio metadata. Inspect readiness, request_coverage, selected input versions and gaps. Briefs are evidence packets, not finished creative concepts or outreach. `save_brief` freezes the server-compiled output, and `read_brief` retrieves that snapshot without recompilation. Newer evidence can supersede a snapshot without rewriting it; withdrawn evidence or removed scope can withhold its payload. All three actions return 200.

### Link retained evidence

`attach_evidence` links one exact retained `source_version_id` to 1–100 distinct existing targets: an artist, a professional, or a Context request/subject pair. Supply a stable `idempotency_key`; retry only the same version and targets with that key. Authentication supplies the actor. The receipt records relevance only; it does not confirm identity, rights or a business mandate. It creates no roster entry and makes no provider/model call or charge.

`read_evidence_attachment` reads one receipt by `attachment_id`. `list_evidence_attachments` reads a page for an exact source version. Pass `next_id` as `after_id` while `has_more` is true, including an empty page where protected receipts were withheld. Reads check current workspace access, source retention and independent target access. Evidence responses and domain errors are private and must not be cached. A later source version needs a separate association; these actions do not rewrite historical receipts. They require the matching evidence-association database and API release; accepted request syntax is not hosted availability.

### Scope and failures

Authentication determines the account. Optional organization_id selects an authorized organization workspace; request and subject ownership are checked again by the operation. Invalid request syntax returns 400, missing authentication 401, rejected organization access 403, and operation conflicts, unavailable evidence or disabled verification 409. No action accepts a caller-supplied account identity. Local schema tests do not establish hosted availability.

### MCP mapping

Standard MCP uses the `context` tool with the same action and fields as this REST request. The three evidence actions also have individually discoverable object-schema tools listed separately below; they are excluded from delegated OAuth connections. Delegated OAuth exposes the named tools below and supplies the action server-side; omit action from the named tool input. These registrations require the full `mcp:tools` grant, current ownership and fresh credential verification. Read-only is a tool annotation, not a guarantee of hosted readiness. get.description: Returns metadata and status for the current unclaimed, unexpired guest session. Guest access ends when claimed. Unclaimed work expires after seven days.

401.description: Guest session or account authentication missing.

409.description: Operation unavailable; retry the same input and session.

post.description: Requires the original guest cookie plus verified account authentication. Optionally claims into an authorized organization. Transfers saved metadata without refetching it; an in-progress worker finishes into the claimed destination. Repeated claims by the same account and destination return the same request ID. Another account cannot claim it. Existing matching identities and customer corrections are preserved. No artist ownership claim is implied. Signup UI integration must call this endpoint after authentication. The Recoup app provides a /context entry page and claims into the personal account after login. A failed extraction remains retryable through the same claim receipt. No completion email or website is generated by this flow.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: The configured funnel origin. This is a browser session flow, not a public unauthenticated MCP tool.
